hook_patterns: Open with a concrete battle/map outcome before explaining the cause
Ask a sharp historical question in the first line (Could X have been stopped?)
Lead with one archaeological object or ruin that proves a larger claim
Start with a first-hand reaction or primary-source shock detail
Name a place + year immediately so the viewer knows the stakes
tone: Documentary-confident. Specific names, dates, and places. Dramatic without clickbait spam. Evidence-first.
pacing: 50-59s shorts: hook in 0-2s, one clear claim, one visual beat change every 3-5s, payoff before end. Longs: chaptered story with primary-source texture.
structure: Hook question/claim → map or artifact establish → rising stakes → evidence reveal → consequence/why it still matters
forbidden: don't forget to like and subscribe

script_instructions: Prefer How/Why/Could question titles. Use maps, labeled leaders, and artifact close-ups. Keep Shorts near 50-55s when possible. End on consequence, not a soft summary.

shorts: Vertical 9:16 map with parchment texture and empire color blocks
Large serif labels for empires; small labels for cities
Portrait callout cards for key figures mid-video
Motion: slow push/pan on maps every few seconds
High contrast text; avoid cluttered lower-third spam
longs: Documentary stills with gentle Ken Burns
Evidence captions tied to narration claims
visual_dna.thumbnail_style: One strong artifact or map detail + short readable subject words; earthy scholarly palette
